title: tidy-paths-refactor-idea-log
content:
Context:
- Scratchpad for small-path refactor ideas discovered while reviewing PRs that touch route resolution and module imports. Goal is to reduce accidental long import chains and make ownership boundaries clearer without a big-bang rewrite.

High-level hypothesis:
- Moving a thin "utils/path-normalizer" layer closer to request routing will make it easier to reason about path normalization and avoid subtle double-normalize bugs seen in PR #4187.
- Keep surface area small: introduce adapter functions rather than moving entire modules. Defer full module split until telemetry shows hotspots.

Quick checklist (pre-PR):
- [ ] Add unit tests for edge-case path inputs (double-slash, trailing dot, mixed-case windows-style)
- [ ] Add property test (randomized-ish) for round-trip normalize -> join -> normalize invariants
- [ ] Ensure all callers import via new adapter rather than direct util where possible
- [ ] Add a small e2e harness that runs representative routes against a local rack of services (script below)

Runnable harness (local) - rough:
- ./scripts/mini-route-harness --workers=2 --seed=42 --routes=sample_routes.json
- sample_routes.json should include fuzzed paths from tests/fuzz/paths.txt

PR surface notes (what to mention in PR description):
- Motivation + small examples of failures fixed (copy a short failing input -> expected output)
- Compatibility: adapter is a no-op by default for callers that pass already-normalized paths
- Backwards-compatible: describe fallback behavior for legacy callers (link INF-1023 for longer discussion)
- Rollout plan: canary 5% on dedicated -> 25% -> 100% with auto-rollback on 2xx->4xx spike or latency regression > 20%

Risk matrix (quick):
- Low: cosmetic changes, tests catch most cases
- Medium: mis-normalize leads to cache misses (KV cache hit-rate drop) -> check kv-cache hit-rate metric per-route for first 6h post-deploy
- High: path changes change auth-scoped keys -> ensure auth tests run and token-scoped scenarios included in e2e harness

Open questions / things to verify before merge:
- Who owns the area: route-resolvers or platform-http? (talk to @Marcus for final ownership)
- Do we need to add migration note for internal clients that rely on previous normalization quirks? (INF-1023 has initial notes)
- Are there any external integrations (private deployments) that depend on prior behavior? Log a quick audit: search GH for "normalizePath(" across private-deployments packages.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Short lived post-merge playbook to watch for:
  - kv_cache.route_hit_rate (per-route) - create a dashboard tile and alert if drop > 15% vs baseline
  - per-route 4xx rate monitor for first 3 deploy windows
  - sampling of request traces that show normalized vs un-normalized path keys
- If we see sustained hit-rate drop: revert adapter and ship flag to gate usage per-service
- If stable, schedule a cleanup sprint to move callers to import from the adapter explicitly and remove legacy util in two quarters

Notes to self (TODOs while drafting code):
- Inline comment pattern: explain why we intentionally preserve trailing slash for X endpoints (customers rely on it)
- Add a small `normalize_preserving_trailing_slash` helper instead of toggling flags at callsite
- Keep the new module tiny (< 150 lines) and well-documented with examples in module docstring

Local checklist before request for review (internal to me):
- [ ] Run `make test` and `make lint` locally
- [ ] Run harness for 60s and inspect sampled traces
- [ ] Draft PR description with rollback plan + runbook snippet
- [ ] Add reviewers: Marcus Li (owner), Evelyn Shaw (SRE), and one ETA from console team (TBD)

Snippet: minimal adapter pseudo-code to paste into PR description:
```
// adapter: utils/path_adapter.go
func NormalizeForRouting(p string) string {
  // canonicalize separators, collapse duplicate slashes, but preserve trailing slash for endpoints marked as "strictTrailing"
  // small, well-tested, dependency-free
}
```

Quick thought: keep this small and iteratively expand if telemetry shows edges. Large refactors look nice but increase blast radius.

If I get time: add a small fuzz-run on CI that exercises path-normalize across recent commits (last 20) and fail the job if any new input flips the canonicalization behavior (guard rails).

-- Sanjana
